surprises.title: Paint peels in sheets
surprises.description: You scrape one flake, and a whole sheet peels off like a sunburn.

options.text: Paint right over it
Scrape, sand, and prime
Strip the whole room to bare drywall

surprises.title: Lead paint shows up
surprises.description: The house is from 1955, and the test swab just turned red.

options.text: Power-sand it smooth
Use lead-safe prep with wet sanding
Hire abatement for the whole house

surprises.title: Cracks keep returning
surprises.description: Diagonal cracks above the door. You patched them last year. They're back.

options.text: Have the framing and header checked
Fill with flexible caulk and repaint
Underpin the foundation

surprises.title: Nail pops appear
surprises.description: Little round bumps everywhere. The drywall nails are backing out.

options.text: Drive screws beside them and patch
Paint over the bumps
Replace all the drywall

surprises.title: Water stain appears
surprises.description: Under the old paint, a brown ring near the ceiling. That water came from somewhere.

options.text: Find the leak before painting
Cover it with stain-blocking primer only
Replace the whole ceiling

surprises.title: Mold shows up
surprises.description: Behind the dresser, the wall is speckled with mold.

options.text: Fix the moisture source and clean it
Use mold-resistant paint over it
Gut the room

surprises.title: Outlet is scorched
surprises.description: You take off an outlet cover, and the outlet behind it is black and melted.

options.text: Paint around it and leave it
Power off, replace the outlet
Rewire the room

surprises.title: Wallpaper hides underneath
surprises.description: The "paint" is actually painted-over wallpaper. And it's bubbling.

options.text: Replace all the drywall
Strip the wallpaper and skim coat
Glue down the bubbles and paint

surprises.title: Color looks wrong
surprises.description: The swatch said "Soft Sage." The wall says "Hospital Hallway."

options.text: Test samples in daylight before choosing
Live with it
Repaint the room three more times

surprises.title: Trim paint won't stick
surprises.description: The new latex peels off the trim with a fingernail. The old trim paint is oil-based.

options.text: Scuff and use a bonding primer
Add another coat
Replace all the trim

surprises.title: Window gets painted shut
surprises.description: The window you painted around is now sealed tight.

options.text: Pry it open with a screwdriver
Cut the paint seal with a window zipper
Replace the window

surprises.title: Ceiling looks dingy
surprises.description: The fresh walls make the ceiling look yellow and tired.

options.text: Leave it for another day
Install a drop ceiling
Paint the ceiling too

surprises.title: Whole house looks dull
surprises.description: This room looks amazing. The rest of the house, less so.

options.text: Plan the next room for next month
Paint just the parts guests see
Paint the whole house this week

surprises.title: Accent wall idea strikes
surprises.description: What if one wall had board-and-batten? Or wallpaper? Or both?

options.text: Add board-and-batten to every room
Save it for after this job
Draw the battens on with a marker

surprises.title: Partner requests shelves
surprises.description: Your partner: "Since the walls are fresh, can we put up floating shelves?"

options.text: Build a full built-in library
Let the paint cure, then hang them
Hang them now on the wet paint

video.title: Paint a room like a pro

ask.question: How do I paint a room?
ask.answer: Fun project! 1. Buy paint. 2. Paint the walls. 3. Admire!
ask.skipped: It skipped taping, primer and the second coat.
